title: Encoded state length bound
statement: Let $z$ be a finite bit string and let $s=(R,d,m,rc)$ consist of a list of rows of natural numbers and three natural numbers. Decode the first component of $z$ using the aligned pair parser, taking the empty word if parsing fails, and let its binary value be $p$. Suppose $R$ has length $m	ext{,}$ has at most $|z|$ rows, each row has length at most $|z|$, every entry of every row is less than $p+2^{|z|}+2$, $d<p+2^{|z|}+2$, and $rc	ext{≤}m$. Then the bit string obtained by encoding $p$ and the state $s$ has length at most $64(|z|+1)^3$.
